doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Advice and favorite eras of jazz
summary: Advice to study everything, and the bebop era as his favorite.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: What’s your advice to a young trumpet player who aspires to what you do.

Well just study all you can. You know when I was a kid there was just — here in Los Angeles there was just Chet Baker and Conte Candoli and me, and not so many others that were right here that lived here. And now there’s hundreds of guys that are sensational. They do everything. And you’ve got to study everything you can about music. Because all the kids I’ve got in my band they can read anything and they have all played jazz and the musician caliber is up high. Well you know from teaching, don’t you think?

Oh yeah, the kids are good boy. I’ve got a drummer, Ray Brinker, he graduated from Texas, North Texas, they’ve had a lot of good people come out of there. And he can read anything. He plays great. This guy’s one of the best I’ve ever heard.
Is there let’s say a decade, a ten year span, where the music of that ten year span was really a favorite for you?

Yeah I think when Charlie Parker started and Dizzy Gillespie and Count Basie was going, Lester Young. Maybe the 30s and 40s, back. I don’t know, well then Miles came along. It’s all good, it keeps going, it gets going fast for me though with a lot of the real modern guys. But I guess I’m getting a little older. I love the rhythm music. I love the bebop. That was so new. And I don’t think — nobody that I’ve heard plays much better © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

than Charlie Parker. Oh but Louis Armstrong too, nobody plays better than him really, you hear the records he made, that guy. And then these new kids, what is it Roy Hargrove, he’s great too. There’s just all kinds of talent.
